children: Defence stocks are in focus on Tuesday, September 8, as brokerage firm Motilal Oswal reiterated its positive stance on the sector after the Defence Acquisition Council's (DAC) recent proposal approvals.

The brokerage has "buy" ratings on Bharat Electronics Ltd (BEL),Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) and Astra Microwave Products Ltd (AMPL) with target prices indicating an upside of up to nearly 31%. It said BEL remains its preferred pick.
DAC approvals
The DAC on Monday, September 7, approved the acceptance of necessity (AoNs) for various acquisition proposals worth ₹1.1 lakh crore for the Indian Army, Navy and Air Force.

The approvals focus on mine warfare, battlefield mobility, chemical biological radiological and nuclear (CBRN) protection, surveillance, electronic warfare and naval propulsion, with 98% of the total AoNs earmarked for the Indian industry, the brokerage said.

The DAC has given approvals worth ₹1.62 lakh crore so far in this fiscal, taking the total approvals to ₹13 lakh crore over financial year 2025-2027. Motilal Oswal said that this enhances the total addressable market of domestic players.

The Centre has also been taking steps to open missile production to Indian private players. These initiatives improve order inflow visibility for the defence sector, Motilal Oswal said, adding that in the near to medium term, finalisation of large tenders for defence PSUs should be keenly watched out for.

Among the recent approved proposals, Motilal Oswal is the view that BEL is a potential beneficiary for the CBRN recce vehicles for the Indian Army, Arudhra radars for the Indian Navy, and ground-based multi-purpose jammer for the Indian Air Force.

Meanwhile, it named HAL as the only potential beneficiary for the advanced light helicopters proposal for the Indian Army. It also named it as one of the potential beneficiaries for the marine gas turbines for the Indian Navy.
Motilal Oswal added that Astra Microwave Products could be a potential beneficiary for the ground-based multi-purpose jammer proposal for the Indian Air Force.
These Are Motilal Oswal's 'Buy' Recommendations
Motilal Oswal has a target price of ₹530 per share on
BEL

, which indicates an upside of 30.7% from its previous close. It said BEL currently trades at 42.2x, 36.2x and 32.2x its estimated FY27, FY28 and FY29 earnings per share (EPS), respectively. The brokerage's price target on BEL values the stock at 45 times its two-year forward earnings.
The brokerage has a target price of ₹5,800 apiece for
HAL

, which indicates an upside of 19.5%. It said the stock trades at 32.4x, 27x and 22.3x its estimated FY27, FY28 and FY29 EPS, respectively. HAL's target price is based on the average of discounted cash flow (DCF) and 30x two-year forward earnings.

Motilal Oswal has a target price of ₹1,900 per share on AMPL, which indicates an upside of 10.1%. It said the stock trades at 66.3x, 48.5x and 34.4x its estimated FY27, FY28 and FY29 EPS, respectively. Its target price values the stock at 42x two-year-forward earnings, the brokerage said.

Stock reactions
BEL shares ended the previous session flat at ₹405.5 apiece. The stock has gained 0.3% in the past month and is up 2% this year, so far.
HAL shares ended the previous session flat at ₹4,852 apiece. The stock has declined 1.5% in the past month but is up 10.3% in 2026, so far.
AMPL shares ended the previous session 0.2% lower at ₹1,725 apiece. The stock is down 0.6% in the past month but up 75.5% this year, so far.

title: Three defence stocks that Motilal Oswal recommends buying after the latest DAC proposals
